origin: cwe/125/c Key Principles: use strnlen() rather than strlen() on buffers not guaranteed to contain NUL within their allocation

finding.name: Out-of-bounds Read
finding.summary: A fixed-size record name buffer is treated as a NUL-terminated string; if no NUL exists in the 16-byte field, strlen() reads into following memory.

trap: Adding a terminator after the strlen() call, switching to strnlen() but accepting a result equal to the field capacity as a valid complete name, or checking sizeof(record->name) after it has decayed to a pointer in a helper. The fix must bound the scan to the actual field size and reject missing terminators if the format requires one.
must_preserve: Names with a NUL inside the 16-byte field still report their existing length, unterminated names fail closed or report invalid data, and the flags field is never read as part of the name.
